posts.title: Turn long PDFs into searchable text
posts.promise: A small workflow can extract selected pages and return readable markdown.
posts.whatItIs: The example is an n8n template for processing large documents with an external extraction service and Gemini. It uploads a file, checks an asynchronous job until it finishes, then retrieves page data for OCR and conversion to markdown. A student version could accept one PDF and return selected pages as text.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: small research or operations teams that process long PDFs might pay for a dependable document conversion service. The supplied template gives no evidence that these buyers exist or will pay.
loop: Receive a PDF and the pages requested.
Send the file to the extraction service.
Check the job status on a schedule until complete.
Retrieve only the requested page data.
Convert the returned content to markdown.
Show the output and flag failures for a person to review.
posts.evidence: The n8n template page describes an Extract API upload, files up to 100 MB, a returned job record, polling through the Jobs endpoint, and retrieving dataset items; it says the example sends pages through a multimodal model to parse markdown. This establishes a documented workflow example, not customer outcomes.
posts.uncertainty: The example requires an external Subworkflow.ai API key and Gemini setup; fees, reliability, rights to submitted documents, and customer demand are not established here. A student version should limit file size and pages, avoid sensitive documents, and have a person review OCR errors. The source does not show that the original business runs without operator oversight.
first24Hours: Import the public n8n template and map the documented steps on paper.
Use a short, non-sensitive sample PDF to check upload, job polling, and text retrieval.
Ask two people who handle long PDFs whether page selection and markdown output solve a real task; record feedback without claiming demand.
